title: Finite-Tor domains and Hom bijections for the tensor–Hom chain
statement:
Fix the scheme and four coefficient-stage conventions of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes, with the exceptional adjunction supplied as in [fix-prop-adjunctions]. Let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and $N\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. Use the derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the chosen restricted tensor–Hom adjunction [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-adjunctions], and the projection isomorphism [fix-prop-projection-formula] with its map specified in [def-exchange-projection]. Put
$$C=Rf_!M,\qquad L_N=R\mathcal Hom_X(M,Rf^!N),\qquad A_N=Rf_*L_N,\qquad B_N=R\mathcal Hom_Y(C,N).$$
Integral pullback and tensor are completed; field operations use rationalization and common finite coefficient stages. For every $T\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, the objects $C$, $A_N$, $B_N$ lie in $D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, and $Rf^!N$, $L_N$, $Lf^*T$, $M\otimes^LLf^*T$ lie in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. In particular $P_{A_N}$ is defined and is an isomorphism. The following are bijections of Hom sets on these full subcategories:
$$\operatorname{Hom}_Y(T,A_N)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_X(Lf^*T,L_N)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_X(M\otimes^LLf^*T,Rf^!N)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!(M\otimes^LLf^*T),N)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_Y(C\otimes^LT,N)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_Y(T,B_N).$$
The first and third are respectively the inverse ordinary and exceptional adjunction bijections; the second is inverse tensor–Hom adjunction with left factor $M$; the fourth is precomposition with $P_T$; the fifth is tensor–Hom adjunction with left factor $C$.

proof.text: Use the supplied PodCtfAdjunctionData R of [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-adjunctions]. Every displayed object is already an object of the indicated finite-Tor full subcategory: support, direct, exceptional and pull return objects of those categories; the restricted Hom functors of [def-pod-ctf-pairing-maps] and the chosen tensor do likewise. Extract the property field of each of the seven objects. This uses the supplied preservation data, rather than re-proving stability at each coefficient stage.

proof.text: The map P at A_N is by definition the hom of PodCtfPairing.projectionIso from [def-pod-ctf-pairing-maps], hence is an isomorphism. For the first, second and third Hom maps use bijectivity of the inverse equivalences R.ordinaryAdjunction.homEquiv, (R.tensorAdjunctionX M).homEquiv and R.exceptionalAdjunction.homEquiv, evaluated at exactly the displayed objects. For the fifth use bijectivity of (R.tensorAdjunctionY (R.support.obj M)).homEquiv in its forward direction. These are the specified fully faithful restricted adjunctions of [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-adjunctions].

source.place: Step 1, reversed Hom chain on the supplied restricted categories

proof.text: For the fourth map let p=PodCtfPairing.projectionIso at (M,T), so the specified map is v ↦ p.hom ≫ v. If two images agree, precompose that equality with p.inv and use associativity and p.inv ≫ p.hom = 1 to recover equality of the inputs. Given v in the target, its preimage is p.inv ≫ v; associativity and p.hom ≫ p.inv = 1 prove that its image is v. Combine this bijectivity with the preceding seven memberships, isomorphism and four bijections by conjunction introduction.
